content.rationale:
Five prerequisites each fix one side of one document — where the registry is (nolspvpw), that a record is one JSON document at `.deccy/work/<handle>.json` found by scanning (rqtowtqn), that it is keyed by a generated handle and names one target node, one edit and one workspace by name and path (kwqnrzoz), that it is `open` until its draft lands and `landed` thereafter and retained (yuomrusm), and that it carries a content-identity base of the node's owned set as a per-path map of content-determined values (qrqsxyzz) — and none settles what a conforming record document is. `twpvqstu` says so explicitly: which fields the object carries, and in what version, is a separate commitment. This decision is that commitment, and it is made as a machine-checkable artifact rather than prose so every writer and reader of the registry checks the same document shape: `schemas/work.json` is the record's form, and the note that the artifact enforces shape and not meaning is the same note the house schemas carry — the schema judges the document, never the validity of what its strings point at.

The field set is exactly the record's form and nothing else: `handle`, `state`, `node`, `edit`, `workspace`, `base`. The handle is the key `kwqnrzoz` mints for the record; `state` is the state `yuomrusm` gives it; `node`, `edit` and `workspace` are the three references `kwqnrzoz` names and `owyntkvw` calls the whole of a record's references; `base` is the content-identity base `qrqsxyzz` places beside them in the same document. Nothing else is admitted because a field the record's form does not carry would be a second place for a record's state to live, and `twpvqstu` settles that no part of a record is kept anywhere but that one document. The object is therefore closed at both levels: an unknown key at the top is refused, and so is an unknown key inside `workspace`.

No `version` field. `twpvqstu` leaves the field set and the version to a separate commitment, and the prerequisites name no version value for this document; adding one here would be a field, and a requiredness, that no prerequisite states as part of the record's form. If a version stamp is wanted it is its own commitment, and the schema can grow the field without any of the five prerequisites moving.

The handle is a non-empty string and no more. `kwqnrzoz` mints it and `szvotxpq` generates it, so the value space is the opening's rule and not this schema's; a pattern or length rule chosen here would either encode one generator's format into every reader or refuse handles a later generator may mint. What the schema can state is that the field is one string, present, and non-empty because the same string is the document's filename stem (`rqtowtqn`) and an empty stem names no file. That the handle is not a node id, not a change id and not derived from either is a rule about minting, not about the shape of the string, and it stays with the model.

`state` is an enum of `open` and `landed` because those are the two values `yuomrusm` gives the record. The one-way transition and the retention of a landed record are not properties of a document: they are rules over the record's life, unrepresentable in JSON Schema, and they stay with the lifecycle model the requirement is read from. The schema fixes which values a record may carry; it does not pretend to fix which one it may move to.

`node` and `edit` are each one non-empty string, not arrays. `kwqnrzoz` says the record names exactly one target node and exactly one edit, and an array field would let one record name several, so the arity is carried by the field's type and not by a length constraint. Neither field takes an id pattern: the node's addressing is the graph's rule (`xwyryumr` and the node schema), and the edit's id space is fixed nowhere in these prerequisites, so a pattern here would be a rule this decision invents. The journal's `target` is the house precedent — a bare non-empty string for a change reference — and it is followed deliberately.

`workspace` is a nested closed object with `name` and `path` both required. `kwqnrzoz` says the workspace is named by name and path, which is two values, and nesting them keeps the workspace one reference among the three rather than splitting it into two more top-level fields. Both are required because a draft is written in its own workspace and the name alone does not say where it is written. The path is a bare non-empty string: whether it is absolute, what it is relative to and what lives under it are workspace rules settled elsewhere, and pinning a shape here would refuse a path that rule permits.

`base` is an object keyed by repo-relative path whose every entry is unconstrained. `qrqsxyzz` places the base in this one document as a value per path of the node's owned set, which is enough to fix the map and its path keys; it deliberately does not fix the encoding — the algorithm, length and textual form of a content identity — so the schema must not fix it either. `additionalProperties: true` is the honest rendering: the map's presence, its keys and its being one field of one document are the record's form, while the entry's value space belongs to the model. A `oneOf` of hex-or-null copied from the journal would be exactly the kind of borrowed strictness this field must not have. The keys are non-empty strings because they are paths, and a path names something; the owned set, the comparison and the moment the base is read are model rules and stay with them.

`$id` is `urn:deccy:schema:work`, on the same absolute namespace as the node, marker and journal schemas, because the binary's validator compiles a schema only under an absolute identifier and because the artifact is meant to be the one carried by the CLI rather than a document read from the repository. The file carries no verdict and no evidence: it describes the document's form, and the finding that it matches or diverges from the prerequisites belongs to the evaluation that checks it.
